articles.title: Week 6: Summary
articles.meta: Sun 6th September 2026 | Match Reviews | By Martin Fallon
articles.body:
EMIRATES FA CUP

The NWCFL had just three teams remaining in the Emirates FA Cup as the First Qualifying Round took place, and all three will be in the hat for Monday's draw following their results on Saturday.

Trafford travelled to Bamber Bridge who play two divisions higher in the Northern Premier League Premier Division, and trailed by a solitary goal at the break. Ten minutes into the second half Lewis Jacklin levelled the tie, with Dillon Edmundson putting Trafford ahead with just under 20 minutes to go. Bridge pushed for an equaliser and were caught in stoppage time when Trafford were awarded a penalty, with Edmunson converting to give his side a 3-1 win and a place in the next round.

The other two sides faced each other as South Liverpool took on Prestwich Heys. Jack Bentley put South ahead on 26 minutes but it was level at the break with Luke Findlow replying before half time. South then regained the lead ten minutes into the second half thanks to Owen Dursley, and it looked like South were good value for a place in the next round. That was until two minutes into stoppage time when Ellis Richardson found another equaliser for Heys, with a 2-2 draw meaning a replay is required on Tuesday evening.

PREMIER DIVISION .

Glossop North End are the new leaders in the Premier Division after a convincing win away at Longridge Town. An Alex Bowker double put them two goals ahead in the first 20 minutes with Longridge pulling one back before half time. The second half though was one way traffic with five goals scored by Glossop without reply to give them a 7-1 win. Ethan Sutcliffe scored the last two goals to give himself a brace also.

Level on points with Glossop are Chadderton, who won 1-0 at FC St Helens thanks to Jordan Lazenbury's goal 20 minutes from time. That's three consecutive wins for Chaddy now, all without conceding a goal.

Newly promoted Nelson are just a point off the pace after a 6-1 home win against AFC Liverpool. Sefton Gonzales scored twice in the opening 17 minutes to put the Admirals in control, with Luke Hepple helping himself to a second half hat-trick as his team went six goals up. Liverpool's consolation came in stoppage time from the penalty spot.

Burscough are fourth after being held to a 1-1 draw at FC Isle of Man. They went ahead through Caleb Jones goal after just three minutes, with Charlie Higgins levelling for the Ravens with a minute to go. They are sixth in the table, one of three clubs on 12 points.

The final play-off spot at present is held by Droylsden who ran out 2-0 winners in their local derby match with Abbey Hey.

Irlam ran out 2-0 winners at home to Ramsbottom United, with Barnoldswick Town winning 1-0 at Charnock Richard. The final game saw Litherland REMYCA and Euxton Villa play out a goalless draw.

FIRST DIVISION NORTH

It was a big day for AFC Knowsley who played their first game at home since coming up to the NWCFL against Ashville. Benjamin Taylor scored their first home goal after just eight minutes with Daniel Bulayima adding to it ten minutes later. Ashville pulled one back before half time through Ben Greenop, and it proved vital with the Villians going on to hit three goals in the second half to complete a fine 4-2 comeback win.

Maghull remain top but wasted a glorious opportunity to increase their lead as they went down 1-0 at Thornton Cleveleys. The Flyde Coats side are up to second, four points behind Maghull, with Ben Duffield getting the only goal after just 18 minutes.

Cammell Laird 1907 are seemingly enjoying life in the North, consolidating third place after a 2-1 home win against Daisy Hill. Darwen and Holker Old Boys make up the play-off spots and are just a point behind Lairds. Darwen beat Garstang 3-2, Kalvin Morris with a brace for Darwen with Kit Lloyd hitting a late winner. Holker lost the chance to move higher as they went down 4-1 at home to Maine Road, Calvin Harper hitting two goals in stoppage time for the visitors.

Ashton Athletic led Halewood Apollo 2-0 after 20 minutes thanks to Josh Nicholson's brace. However Halewood turned it around and hit the winner in the 89th minute through Charlie Glennon. Another game sealed late on was Colne's win at Squires Gate, with Barney Wiggin scoring his side's second goal in stoppage time to give them a 2-0 win.

Cian Donohue scored twice as Flixton beat Steeton 3-1 with Kaiden Barlow also scoring twice for Bacup Borough in their 2-1 win over AFC Blackpool. Ashton Town beat Uppermill 2-0, with Fulwood Amateurs winning 1-0 against Woolton.

FIRST DIVISION SOUTH

Leaders AFC Bridgnorth romped to the biggest win of the day in the First Division South, a 4-0 home win against Shawbury United making it six wins from seven games. They are a point ahead of the chasing pack with a game in hand on all of them.

That chasing pack sees Sandbach United in second just a point behind, and they had Robbie Hatton to thank for a 1-0 win at Brereton Social, that goal coming two minutes into stoppage time.

Eccleshall are third after a 3-2 win over Dawley Town, with Stafford Town and Wolverhampton Casuals a point further back to complete the play-off spots. Stafford beat Allscott Heath 2-1 at home, whilst Casuals saw Kieran Cook hit a hat-trick in their 3-3 draw with Bilston Town. Bilston led that game early on before Cook put his side two goals ahead, however Bilston hit back for a point.

It was a case of never leave early at Market Drayton Town in their game with Cheadle Heath Nomads. Drayton led 1-0 until 20 minutes from time when Nomads levelled. Nomads then went ahead in the 88th minute through Chigozie Ewelike before Oliver Griffiths levelled two minutes later. Shaun Rowley then made a stunning save to keep Nomads out before Durell Manhertz hit a stoppage time winner for Drayton.

Another 3-2 win came at Wednesfield Community who beat Telford Town. Wednesfield went ahead before Telford turned things around, and it was 2-2 at the break. However a late winner from Tyler Bishop gave Wednesfield all three points.

Barnton led Foley Meir 2-1 but had to settle for a point with another late goal, Luke Lewis rescuing a point for Foley three minutes into stoppage time.

The final game saw Crewe win 1-0 at Alsager Town, an Own Goal the difference between the two sides.

PHOTO

Today's photo is from AFC Knowsley's first home game in the NWCFL against Ashville.

articles.title: Week 6: Preview
articles.meta: Fri 4th September 2026 | Match Previews | By Ben Wilkinson
articles.body:
PREMIER DIVISION

Charnock Richard vs Barnoldswick TownCharnock Richard come into the weekend in 9th position and are now unbeaten in their last three, while Barnoldswick sit in 13th with as many as five draws to their name already this term. Charnock seem to have Barlick's number, winning 14 of the 18 games between the pair! The visitors from East Lancashire will aim to buck the trend and secure a first win at Mossie Park since February 2018.

Droylsden vs Abbey HeyIt's a local derby at the Butchers' Arms where Droylsden welcome rivals Abbey Hey. The Bloods started the season off well but have lost two of their last three in all competitions, whilst Abbey Hey have yet to taste victory this season and have shipped six goals in a game on no fewer than three occasions already.

FC St Helens vs ChaddertonFC St Helens have had a middling start to the campaign and lie in 12th position, whilst the visitors Chadderton are in 2nd place in their mission to push on after positive seasons since their own promotion. The Stripes had kept four clean sheets in a row before defeat against Charnock Richard midweek and they will need that defensive stability on home soil against an attacking Chady outfit.

Irlam vs Ramsbottom UnitedRamsbottom make the journey round the M60 to Silver Street to take on Irlam on Saturday afternoon. Rammy have had an inconsistent start to life under Rob Henry's premiership but two wins on the bounce suggests that a corner may have been turned as they look to go one better than last time and secure a return to the NPL.

Nelson vs AFC LiverpoolAFC Liverpool have suffered a torrid start to their 2026/27 season, having lost every game to date and as a result they remain rooted to the foot of the table. It's a tall ask for them to turn it around this weekend as they visit The Daisy Arena to face a very impressive Nelson side, who sit 4th in the table with four wins from their opening six. The Admirals, under the stewardship of Arron Ripley, have made a storming start to life in the Premier Division and will see this as a great opportunity to return to winning ways following a narrow reverse against Trafford last time out.

FC Isle of Man vs BurscoughIt's been a positive start to the season for FC Isle of Man after their struggles last time out and they are currently in 7th position, whilst this weekend's visitors to The Bowl, Burscough, sit pretty at the top of the tree and have hit the back of the net 22 times already this term! This is arguably the standout fixture in the Premier Division this weekend with two attacking sides going tooth and nail on Saturday evening.

Other fixtures:

FIRST DIVISION NORTH

AFC Knowsley vs AshvilleIt's a long awaited first NWCFL home game for AFC Knowsley and they come into this momentous occasion with 7 points from their opening 8 games (all away from home). The first visitors to the Lord Derby Pavilion are Ashville, who with a record of 3-3-3 from their 9 games to date are the definition of consistently inconsistent! Ashville's last game was their first of the season where they kept a clean sheet, whilst they have scored in every match-up so far - expect more goals here!

Ashton Town vs UppermillUppermill have struggled following promotion and currently bring up the rear of the pack with just three points and no wins. Their hosts on Saturday started in similar fashion, losing their opening six, before three wins on the bounce propelled them up the table. With another home game here, Town will be aiming to make it four and further compound Uppermill's miserable opening to life on the pitch in the NWCFL.

Darwen FC vs GarstangTwo Lancastrian sides with opposing starts to the season do battle at the Anchor Ground. Hosts Darwen have taken 14 points from their 7 games and lie just outside the playoff spots whilst Garstang look set for another season of struggle after picking up just four points so far. The Salmoners have notched 11 times in their last four and will seek to keep that firepower up front active.

Flixton vs SteetonIt's a first ever competitive meeting between these two as Steeton make the journey over to Manchester to take on Flixton at Valley Road. The league table would make the hosts firm favourites but the visiting Chevvies are more than capable of turning on the style and upsetting the applecart on their day.

Fulwood Amateurs vs WooltonFulwood, despite scoring 11 in their last four, haven't taken the win in any of them as a leaky defence has proved their undoing thus far whilst their opponents on Saturday boast one of the meanest back lines in the division with 10 goals conceded and just one defeat. Fulwood's home advantage may prove to be the difference in a finely-poised encounter.

Ashton Athletic vs Halewood ApolloHalewood Apollo attempt to return to winning ways away at an Ashton Athletic side who are reeling from five successive defeats. Athletic started the season strongly with two wins to nil but are now on a run of seven without success. There's been 29 goals in the 8 league games involving Apollo so form would say this is unlikely to be a dull affair.

Holker Old Boys vs Maine RoadHolker Old Boys lead the chasing pack and thrice came back from two goals down to snatch a draw away at Fulwood Amateurs during the week, next up for them is Maine Road, who make the long trip up to Barrow this weekend. The Brantingham Road side have struggled of late and haven't tasted victory since 11th August; three defeats and a draw since see them in 19th place at this stage.

Thornton Cleveleys vs MaghullMaghull are already an incredible seven points clear after a thunderous start featuring eight wins out of a possible nine. Next in their path is a Thornton Cleveleys side who harbour promotion aspirations of their own and will look to keep a place in the top five throughout the season. These two can't be separated on head-to-head record, with two wins apiece joined by a draw in the two seasons these two have locked horns - including 5-2 victories for both!

Other fixtures:

articles.title: Five Things We Learned 2026/27: Week 5
articles.meta: Thu 3rd September 2026 | Five Things | By Jay Cooper
articles.body:
Another week, another series of matches from the NWCFL. Let's run through the best and worst of what the last week has had to offer.

1. Goals galore on Bank Holiday Monday

There’s little better than watching a football game on a bank holiday, and most fans who attended any NWCFL matches on this past Monday will have gotten their money’s worth. From 14 matches played across the Premier Division and First Division North, a whopping 55 goals were scored, which creates an average of just shy of four goals per game.

Choice cuts include FC Isle of Man hitting Abbey Hey for six without reply, and Irlam edging a six-goal thriller on home soil against Longridge Town in the Prem; and Fulwood Amateurs and Holker Old Boys contesting an eight-goal stalemate, and Darwen winning a seven-goal affair in the 87th minute away at Steeton in the North. Don’t blink!

2. Double-promotion candidates in the Prem?

As of right now, 99% of NWCFL sides have played at least five league games, which has allowed for the pacesetters to emerge. In the Premier Division, Nelson, despite not topping the table, have undeniably thrown their hats into the ring for a potential promotion, which would be their second in as many years if it materialised.

Last season’s Division One North champions won 5-2 at the weekend against winless Abbey Hey, but were beaten by fellow promotion candidates Trafford in midweek. Despite that defeat, they are currently fourth in the table, and are the division’s third-highest top scorers, behind only table-topping Burscough and second-place Chadderton. Watch this space.

3. The late, late show with Max Bardsley-Rowe

Glossop North End were fixed in mid-table throughout the 2025/26 season, but they have made a fantastic start to life in the league for the 2026/27 campaign. Lee Wilshaw’s side took six points from an available six over the course of the bank holiday weekend, seeing off Atherton LR and Droylsden, respectively.

Curiously, the final goal of both games was scored well after the 90th minute, and by the same player for GNE. Max Bardsley-Rowe popped up with a cherry-on-the-cake third in the 92nd minute on Saturday during the 3-0 victory over Rovers; and he scored the decisive goal in a 2-1 win against Droylsden on Monday in the 94th minute of play. Way to play to the whistle, Max!

4. Evans Fortress

Stafford Town have had a bright start to the 2026/27 season, currently sitting in inside of the play-off places in fifth, thanks to their goal difference being three better than nearest challengers New Mills. On Saturday, they were beaten 3-1 on the road by new boys Bilston Town, but they return home this coming weekend for a meeting with another new side in the NWCFL, Dawley Town.

They ought to be optimistic about that upcoming meeting taking place in their own back yard, given that, as of right now, Stafford Town are the last remaining team in the NWCFL to have played at least one home league game, and to not have conceded a league goal on home soil. From three matches thus far, they’ve won 5-0, drawn 0-0, and won 3-0 – more of the same on Saturday?

5. And it begins…

There have been entire seven-day weeks this past summer where it’s been too hot to breathe by the standards of this country, let alone to run around a pitch for 90 minutes. And yet, in the final weekend of August, whilst it was still technically summer, we have had our first postponement in the league for a waterlogged pitch.

The date was August 31st, and the site of the cancellation was Brantingham Road, where Maine Road’s hosting of Garstang was scheduled to take place. Alas, Mother Nature had other ideas on the day – hopefully this is NOT a sign of things to come as summer becomes autumn, and eventually winter.

articles.title: Geoff Wilkinson steps down as NWCFL Vice Chair
articles.meta: Mon 31st August 2026 | Announcements | By Media Team
articles.body:
A change at the top of the League was announced at the AGM last weekend as Vice Chairman and Grading Chairman Geoff Wilkinson has decided to take a step back from his current roles.

Geoff advised League Chairman Chris Stirrup and Secretary John Deal early in January that he would be reducing his time spent on League duties.

He has been involved with the League since 1982 (the very first season!) when he was promoted to Referee on the League. This resulted in a 10 year spell on the League, in addition to 8 years as a linesman on The Football League and 5 years refereeing on the Panel (Conference and Central Leagues).

Following retirement as an active match official (but not forever, more on that later), he also served as Secretary of the North West Counties Football League Referees & Linesman Association, which played its part in giving advice to officials on helping them understand what was required to officiate on the League, this included advice offered by Appointments Officers, League Officials and Managers.

There was a memorable moment back in 2011, as Geoff, then aged 64, took to the field of play as a stand-in linesman during a fixture between Nelson and Daisy Hill. The referee pulled up with an injury inside the opening stages of the match, and once it became clear that he would not be able to continue and the senior assistant referee would have to don the whistle for the remainder of the game, Geoff stepped up from the stands, borrowed the stricken referee's kit, and 'carried the flag' for the bulk of the game.

Geoff was in high spirits when explaining the situation at the time:  "I'm probably the only member of the League Management Committee that still has their own hips and teeth, so it was handy that I was there and able to help out.  After I helped the referee off the pitch, I borrowed his kit, and soon got into the swing of things.

It seemed like most of the first half was down my end, so I had to put the flag up a few times to bring the players down to my speed.  The referee lent me his watch which was fine for the first half, but it was a bit tricky in the second half as I couldn't work out how to reset it at half time.

The match assessor came into the dressing room afterwards, and he was surprised when he found out how old I was.  He said that after watching my performance for 90 minutes, he had thought I was much older than that!

As it turned out, the assistant on the other side of the field on Saturday was only 16.  I don't think there will be many more occasions where you'll get such a difference in age between match officials officiating in our league.”

Aside from his roles officiating the game, Geoff has spent 25 seasons on the League Management Committee; starting as Secretary in 2000, remaining in that post for 7 years, before then coming Grading Chairman and finally took on the role of Vice Chairman 11 seasons ago.

“I have been very fortunate to work under 3 Chairman in my time: Dave Tomlinson, Paul Lawler and Chris Stirrup, and all three have given me full support in my roles.

One of the pleasures of doing the grading for this League has been watching clubs go from playing on flat fields and park pitches to calling football grounds home, where spectators can enjoy the facilities which have been produced by the many volunteers at our clubs. I make no apology for kicking a few backsides to ensure clubs met the required 31st March deadline for the required grading criteria.

The League is recognised as one where the clubs meet the required facilities and often get praise from The FA for how the Management Committee run the League. Maintaining and improving standards is what we have tried to encourage member clubs to achieve.

What is disappointing to finish my tenure as grading chairman is that the FA have allowed some applicant clubs to be allowed past the 31st March deadline, in fact at the AGM this year, two clubs didn’t even meet the entry requirements and one was passed on the morning of the AGM. Not exactly a moment to remember."

Finally Geoff would like to thank all club officials and Management Committee members for helping the League to become one of the best, if not the best, run League at Steps 5 & 6 and for the lasting friendships made over his time involved with the League, he intends to visit matches locally and keep involved if required.

articles.title: Week 5: Manager Quotes
articles.meta: Mon 31st August 2026 | Manager Reactions | By Jay Cooper
articles.body:
Premier Division:

Amidst another busy weekend of action in the NWCFL, Barnoldswick Town showed great resilience to come back from behind more than once in a 3-2 win against table-topping Burscough. Following the game, joint manager Gerry Harrison said: "It was a close game, and we fought hard. Both teams enjoyed good periods throughout.

"Picking up our first three points of the season is testament to the hard work that the lads have put it since Lewis and I have come in. We are a young, new team who are learning all the time and still getting to know each other. We will endeavour to keep improving moving forwards."

Also victorious in the top tier on Saturday were Ramsbottom United, who, by their own high standards, have had a slow start to the 2026/27 league season. They won 4-1 against bottom side AFC Liverpool, after which, manager Rob Henry said: "It was an important three points for us which lifts the mood following a few disappointing results.

"We started the game really well, on the front foot, and that was exactly what we wanted from the players. We maintained the intensity, kept the pressure on the opposition and tried to really take control of the game by scoring more goals in the early stages. Frustratingly, this was followed by a sloppy spell in the game, where we gave the ball away cheaply and provided the opposition with counter attacking opportunities.

"Thankfully, in the second half, we were much better. We were playing better football with more quality and creating some really good opportunities, and but for a coupe of really good saves from their keeper, it could have been more. This is certainly a platform for us to build on leading into Tuesday night, but we still know we have lots of room to improve.

First Division North:

In the North, AFC Blackpool recorded their first competitive win of the new campaign with a 2-1 victory against newly promoted Halewood Apollo. Following the whistle, gaffer John Salanki said: "We’ve been playing some good football and putting in strong performances, but unfortunately, we haven’t always been getting the results our efforts deserved.

"Finally, on Saturday, we changed that with a huge win. Now it’s about building on that result, taking the confidence forward and continuing to improve every single week.

"This squad has so much potential, and I have absolutely no doubt that we will keep getting better as the season goes on."

There were also maximum points taken on the road by free-scoring Flixton. Alex Mortimer's men came away from a six-goal thriller against Ashville with a 4-2 victory, following which he said: "It was a tough, competitive game.

"Ashville were coming into the game on the back of two good wins, but we knew that if we remained patient and kept playing like we know we can, the chances would come - the lads we have at the top end of the pitch will cause problems for anyone! I’m very pleased with the result, and we move on to the next game."

First Division South:

In the South, one of the weekends biggest winners were Barnton, who were uncompromising in their home victory over new boys Wednesfield Community. Lewis Wood's side came away from the game with a 4-0 win, after which he said: "A performance like that has been coming. We’re going to keep grafting away, keep working hard and hopefully there’ll be plenty more results like this to come.

"We’re now five games unbeaten, which is a great platform for the lads to build on. The hard work doesn’t stop, though - we’ll keep pushing, keep improving and keep believing. And now we look forward to three more games at the Creative Hut Stadium. We've got two important league games and an FA Vase tie.

"We want to keep building that momentum and, with the support behind us, hopefully there’s plenty more to come!"

articles.title: Week 5: Summary
articles.meta: Sat 29th August 2026 | Match Reviews | By Martin Fallon
articles.body:
PREMIER DIVISION .

We have a new leader in the Premier Division with Nelson moving to top spot after a 5-2 win over Abbey Hey. Max Cane hit a first half hat-trick to help put them 4-0 ahead at the break, and they increased this lead in the second half before Abbey grabbed two late consolation goals.

Previous leaders Burscough twice led at Barnoldswick Town, but the home side turned things around with Kuda Chingwaro hitting what proved the winner with 18 minutes remaining. That was their first win in seven games. They are now in joint second, one of four teams now on ten points, two points behind Nelson.

Droylsden are fourth after a 3-0 away win at Euxton Villa, with Jordan Barnett scoring twice for the Bloods. And Chadderton are fourth after a 1-0 victory over South Liverpool, Matthew Barlow with the only goal of the game.

The final team on ten points are Glossop North End who have climbed up after a 3-0 win over Atherton LR, the visitors coming into the match on the back of a three game unbeaten run.

The biggest win of the day came for FC St Helens who won away at Longridge Town. Luke Byron and Tom Lawless both scored twice for the Stripes, who won 5-0 away from home for the first time since joining the league.

Ramsbottom United beatr AFC Liverpool 4-1, with Gareth Hill scoring the first and last goals for them. Irlam won 2-1 at Litherland REMYCA to record their first win of the season, with Trafford beating FC Isle of Man 1-0.

The final game saw Prestwich Heys and Charnock Richard draw 1-1.

FIRST DIVISION NORTH

Maghull remain top of the First Division North after a 5-1 win over Maine Road. It was 1-1 until just after the hour there, with Nathan Moffitt and Connor Rankin both scoring twice to make it seven wins on the trot for Maghull.

Cammell Laird 1907 are up to second after a 2-1 win at Ashton Athletic. The home side led until 20 minutes from time, with a brace from Ben Wood giving Lairds all three points.

Thornton Cleveleys slip to third after a 2-2 draw at home to Bacup Borough. It could have been worse with Bacup leading 2-0 with just over ten minutes to go, with a quickfire double rescuing a point for Thornton.

Holker are up to fourth after a 4-2 win over Daisy Hill, with Jamie Hodgson scoring twice for the Cumbrian side. And Halewood Apollo are fifth after losing 2-1 at AFC Blackpool, Alfie Cox with both goals there to end a run of eight games without a win for Blackpool.

Flixton ran out 4-2 winners at Ashville, with Aaron Dwyer scoring twice for them in that game. And Ashton Town ran out 3-1 winners away at Steeton.

Colne were denied a win at Gastang, with the home side scoring in stoppage time to force a 1-1 draw. Fulwood Amateurs also rescued a point in stoppage time with a 3-3 draw at home to Darwen.

The final game also finished 3-3, with nothing to separate Woolton and Squires Gate.

FIRST DIVISION SOUTH

AFC Bridgnorth remain top in the First Division South after twice coming from behind to beat New Mills 3-2. The winning goal came from David Anani with just three minutes to go to complete a fine turnaround.

They are a point clear of three clubs, one of whom is Sandbach United who beat Widnes Town 6-0. There were three goals in each half there, with Kyle Foley grabbing a brace.

Eccleshall are third after a 1-0 win at Cheadle Heath Nomads, with Wolverhampton Casuals fourth after a 2-0 win over Alsager Town.

Making up the top five is Stafford Town, who missed the chance to go joint top after a 3-1 loss at Bilston Town.

Thomas Stanton found the net twice for Barnton as they swept aside Wednesfield Community 4-0, with Dawley Town winning 2-0 away at Shawbury United.

Crewe won for only the second time this season after a 2-1 win at home to Telford Town, with Foley Meir winning by the same scoreline as they beat Brereton Social at home.

Market Drayton Town were the other winners as they won 2-1 at Allscott Heath.

PHOTO

Today's photo is from @Groundhopper75 from Prestwich's home draw with Charnock.

articles.title: Vacancies
articles.meta: Fri 28th August 2026 | Vacancies | By Martin Fallon
articles.body:
Are you looking for a job at one of our clubs? A number of vacancies have arised at a couple of our clubs that you may be interested in.

First Division North side Garstang have two roles, one being a First Team Match Co-ordinator and the other being a Media Assistant.

articles.title: Five Things We Learned 2026/27: Week 4
articles.meta: Thu 27th August 2026 | Five Things | By Jay Cooper
articles.body:
Another week, another series of matches from the NWCFL. Let's run through the best and worst of what the last week has had to offer.

1. And then there were three in the FA Cup

The Emirates FA Cup Preliminary Round was the key feature of the weekend for a total of nine NWCFL sides. Of those nine, three now remain in English Football’s Oldest Cup Competition.

South Liverpool slipped past fellow NWCFL outfit Longridge Town 3-2 away from home; Prestwich Heys overcame stiff resistance from last season’s First Division South runaway champions Runcorn Town on the road, winning 3-1; and Trafford survived a late fightback by Runcorn Linnets to win 3-2, and complete a hat-trick of away victories for the remaining NWCFL sides in the competition.

2. Burscough the team to beat in the Prem?

On Saturday, the Linnets became the first team in the Premier Division this season to record a double-digit points tally - albeit, they have played the joint most league games at this time. To say that they don’t deserve to top the table as we approach September, however, might be blasphemous.

After slowing down over the course of the prior week, Saturday saw Phil Stafford’s team return to their best as they emerged victorious over Abbey Hey in a 6-3 barnstormer of a game, which featured a hat-trick of penalty goals for Callum Laird. You’ve got to win ‘em to score ‘em, and Burscough certainly did that this past weekend.

3. The wait goes on for AFC Liverpool

At the other end of the Premier Division table right now are AFC Liverpool. Last season’s Macron Cup winners knew that 2026/27 would come with an adjustment period after the departure of their long-time gaffer and core squad in the summer, but few could’ve foreseen seven straight defeats in all competitions to begin the campaign.

And yet, here we are. AFC Liverpool are currently propping up the Prem, and they are the only remaining team across the NWCFL who are yet to score a point. They face promotion-battle veterans Ramsbottom United on bank holiday weekend, who were shellshocked by a late Atherton LR comeback last time out – maybe AFC can catch them off guard this Saturday.

4. Maghull lay down the baton

At the time of writing, there are three points separating first from seventh in the Prem, with a fluctuating number of games played by all teams involved – expected early-season uncertainty, then. In the South, just one point separates table-toppers AFC Bridgnorth from sixth placed Sandbach United, with the leaders currently holding a single game in hand on the chasing pack.

Maghull – top of the tree in the First Division North – have no such worries. Seven games into the new campaign, Joe Burns’ side have been nearly perfect, save for an opening day defeat by Darwen FC. They have a three-point headstart on second-placed Thornton Cleveleys at this stage, and a further two points on the next three teams down. It’s early days, but Maghull look like the NWCFL’s most prominent pacesetters right now.

5. GTF In at Widnes Town

A poor start to their maiden season as an NWCFL side has hopefully dropped to its lowest point for Widnes Town after their 7-0 defeat to Allscott Heath on Saturday. In order to turn their fortunes around, the First Division South’s bottom side have opted for a managerial change.

Paul McNally has left the club, and his replacement brings quite a bit of name value with him. This week, the club have appointed local cult hero Gary Taylor-Fletcher as manager. Taylor-Fletcher played for Blackpool and Leicester City in his pro career, and he scored the Seasiders’ first ever Premier League goal. He will hope to bring the same attacking threat he possessed as a player to the Chemics.

articles.title: Lorraine Beavers Visits Thornton Cleveleys
articles.meta: Wed 26th August 2026 | Thornton Cleveleys | By Martin Fallon
articles.body:
Lorraine Beavers, Labour for Blackpool North and Fleetwood, visited Gamble Road to find out more about developments at Thornton Cleveleys and met with club chairman Steve Abbott.

The fact-finding mission centred on the work of the club around community involvement, juniors setup, senior and women's football. Along with developments on, and off, the pitch.

Mrs Beavers was shown around the club facilities including the Salthouse Bar which has just had planning permission for an extension to the room size.

The Member of Parliament for for Blackpool North and Fleetwood was pleased with her introduction to the club.

"I'd just like to say it's amazing, the community must love this area as you've done so much. I can't believe how many pitches you have and the work you do in the community.  I think this area of Thornton is very lucky to have you here.

"It's been a real inspiration to talk people who care for the community and the club itself. I can't wait to visit again. Thank you very much for inviting me today."

Chairman Steve Abbott thanked the MP for visiting.

"It was a great today to have a catchup with Lorraine Beavers, our local MP.   It was good that she made the time to come along and have a look round. She was very impressed with what we are doing for the local community and how many children and adults we have involved with the club.  We also spoke about our journey into supporting disability football at the club.

"Lorraine was very happy with our impact on the local area and is happy to work with us on future projects. It was a very worthwhile visit. She was impressed with what we are doing for the local area including Thornton-Cleveleys and Fleetwood. Hopefully, our relationship will long continue."

articles.title: Emirates FA Cup First Qualifying Round
articles.meta: Mon 24th August 2026 | FA Competition News | By Martin Fallon
articles.body:
The FA have today released the draws for the First Qualifying Round of the Emirates FA Cup.

Of the 19 Premier Division clubs that entered the Emirates FA Cup this season, we are down to just four, with three winning last Saturday and one requiring a midweek replay if they are to join them.

South Liverpool and Prestwich Heys were two of the sides winning on Saturday, and they have been drawn against each other in the First Qualifying Round. South have played just four times this season but have won three and drew one of them. Prestwich have played six times, and after losing their opening day match, are unbeaten in the last five games with three wins and two draws.

They haven't played each other this season yet, but the league game is scheduled just seven days after this cup tie! The draw does mean one of our sides are guaranteed a place in the Second Qualifying Round, but we'd rather they play others so that they could both progress!

Trafford's reward for winning at Runcorn Linnets will be an away trip to another Northern Premier League side, this time travelling to NPL Premier Division side Bamber Bridge. The Preston side have won just one of their opening five league games, and enter the FA Cup at this stage.

It's the first time in nine years that Bamber Bridge have played one of our sides in the FA Cup, although they lost that 2017 clash as Ashton Athletic beat them 2-1.

Litherland REMYCA face a midweek replay at Prescot Cables. Should they win that then they will be at home to with NPL West side 1874 Northwich or Northern League side Horbury Town.

1874 are no strangers to our sides having played in the NWCFL for plenty of years before being laterally moved to the Midland League. They achieved promotion from that league last season via the play-off's and have started the season with a win, a draw and a loss, with a win and draw in the FA Cup.

Horbury Town play in the Northern Counties East and have played just three league games with two wins and a draw. Their only loss from seven games this season came in the FA Vase last weekend.

Horbury have never faced one of our sides in the FA Cup, but have played twice in the FA Vase, both of those games going to penalties.

Ties will be played on Saturday 5th September 2026.

The draw including our sides can be found below:

FIRST QUALIFYING ROUND

SATURDAY 8 AUGUST 2026

WINNERS RECEIVE £2,250

LOSERS RECEIVE £750

1. Bamber Bridge v Trafford

2. Litherland REMYCA or Prescot Cables v 1874 Northwich or Horbury Town

15. South Liverpool v Prestwich Heys

articles.title: Week 3: Summary
articles.meta: Sat 22nd August 2026 | Match Reviews | By Martin Fallon
articles.body:
EMIRATES FA CUP PRELIMINARY ROUND

South Liverpool are through to the First Qualifying Round of the FA Cup for the first time since 1990 after a 3-2 win at Longridge Town. Two goals from Jack Bentley, either side of one from George Clarkson, put them into a three goal lead midway through the second half. Goals from Francis Leather and Ethan Gough made for a tense finale but South held on to progress.

Trafford produced a giant killing with a 3-2 win at NPL side Runcorn Linnets. Ryan Brooke - Linnets' all time leading scorer - and Jensen Bowering put Trafford two ahead at the break David Worrall adding a third at the start of the second half. Linnets reduced the arrears before adding another in stoppage time, but could not find an equaliser.

Prestwich Heys are also through after a fine away win, that a 3-1 victory at Runcorn Town. After a goalless first half, Ellis Richardson and Tobias Green put Heys two goals ahead with Runcorn reducing the arrears with 20 minutes remaining. Matthew Smyth restored the two goal lead to see Heys through.

Litherland REMYCA live to fight another day after a 1-1 draw with NPL side Prescot Cables. Both goals came in first half stoppage time with Prescot going ahead before REMY equalised. The replay is midweek.

Elsewhere Droylsden levelled against Garforth Town with ten minutes remaining before losing 2-1 to a last minute winner. Nelson went down to a narrow 1-0 loss at Witton Albion.

The final game saw Euxton Villa bow out after a 3-2 loss at Lower Breck.

PREMIER DIVISION .

Atherton LR left it late to record a 2-1 victory at home to Ramsbottom United. An own goal midway through the first half put Rammy ahead with Cal Hunter levelling with five minutes to go. Hunter then netted the winner two minutes into stoppage time.

Burscough romped to a 6-3 victory at home to Abbey Hey with Callum Laird grabbing a hattrick for the Linnets. Jordan Darr scored twice for Charnock Richard as they won 3-0 at home to AFC Liverpool.

Glossop North End won 1-0 at home to Chadderton, with the final game finishing goalless between Barnoldswick Town and FC St Helens.

FIRST DIVISION NORTH

Maghull made it six successive wins with a 3-0 win at Garstang. Connor Rankin put them ahead just after the half hour with Jamie Clark adding another from the penalty spot six minutes into the second half. Nathan Peetwon secured the win with the third ten minutes from time.

Ashton Town also ran out 3-0 winners at Maine Road, all the goals there coming in the first half. However the biggest win of the day was from Steeton who won 4-0 at Squires Gate. Joshua Coe and Kevin Gonzalez put them two ahead inside 17 minutes, before adding another two in the second half.

Jacob Ngoy scored twice for Flixton as they beat AFC Blackpool 3-1 at home. Colne were 3-0 winners at home to Uppermill, all the goals there coming in the second half.

Cammell Laird 1907 also scored three as they beat Fulwood Amateurs 3-2. Ben Wood scored twice for Lairds, with Spencer Lucas also scoring two for the visitors.

Jacob Aspinall was another two score twice for Thornton Cleveleys as they won 2-1 at Ashton Athletic. Woolton won by the same scoreline at Daisy Hill, with Ashville being the third side of the day to win 2-1, their winner from Jack Edwards coming in stoppage time.

Bacup Borough drew 1-1 at home to AFC Knowsley, with Holker Old Boys' game with Halewood Apollo also finishing with that scoreline.

FIRST DIVISION SOUTH

The biggest win of the season so far came from Allscott Heath as they beat Widnes Town 7-0. There were six different scorers with Benjamin Summers netting a brace with the opening two goals of the game.

There was a remarkable finale to the game at New Mills where Shawbury United led 2-1 deep into stoppage time. Six minutes into added time, Cameron Tetlow levelled for the Millers before Luc Ferry hit the winner for the home side a minute later.

Sam Preece scored twice for AFC Bridgnorth as they won 3-2 away at Alsager Town, that result moving them to the top of a tight league table, with Callum Parker scoring twice for Stafford Town in their 3-0 home win against Crewe.

Sandbach United cruised to a 4-1 home win over hitheroe leaders Wolverhampton Casuals. Dawley Town won 3-1 at home to Market Drayton Town, with Cheadle Heath Nomads winning 1-0 at Wednesfield Community thanks to Chigozie Ewelike's stoppage time winner.

Eccleshall won 1-0 at Foley Meir, with Bilston Town drawing 1-1 at home with Barnton. The final game saw Rhyce Brown sciore twice for Telford Town, but they were held 2-2 thanks to Samuel Mellor's leveller seven minutes into stoppage time.

PHOTO

Today's photo is from @Groundhopper75 from Glossop North End's victory at home to Chadderton.

articles.title: Five Things We Learned 2026/27: Week 3
articles.meta: Thu 20th August 2026 | Five Things | By Jay Cooper
articles.body:
Another week, another series of matches from the NWCFL. Let's run through the best and worst of what the last week has had to offer.

1. The Isuzu FA Vase is back!

Like the week prior, this past Saturday was dominated by a nationwide domestic cup competition. The FA Vase returned for 2026/27, and 31 NWCFL made their bows in the first qualifying round.

Of those 31, 11 won their matches outright with choice cuts including Eccleshall hammering Allscott Heath 4-0 at home; First Division South side Barnton upsetting the odds in a 3-1 away win against Premier Division Irlam; and Charnock Richard, Atherton LR, Foley Meir and Telford Town all winning in a dreaded penalty shootout.

2. Gate open for the second qualifier

One team that did’nt feature in the weekend’s FA Vase fixture list, despite initially being scheduled to do so, were First Division North outfit Squires Gate. The seaside club were due to welcome Northern Football League side Boro Rangers, but instead, were given a bye into the next round.

The reason for this goes back to early July, when Boro Rangers folded its senior men’s team after, in their own words, “financial and operational challenges made the team unsustainable.” It’s real a shame that this sort of thing continues to happen up and down the football pyramid, especially given how much money there is in football currently. There’s a slim positive in all this for Gate, however, who were automatically granted a place in the second Vase qualifier.

3. Barnoldswick Town know the draw

Barlick are three league games into the new season, and are currently undefeated, which sounds great. Then you look deeper, and you’ll see that they are also winless, and 13th in the table.

Every NWCFL game that Gerry Harrison and Lewis Craig’s men have played thus far has ended honours even. Away at Abbey Hey on the opening day, it finished 2-2; away at Prestwich Heys in their first midweek game of the season, it finished 1-1; and at home to Ramsbottom United on Tuesday, it also finished 1-1. They even drew their FA Cup EP round tie with Atherton Collieries 12 days ago, only to be beaten in the replay.

4. Hard times for Ashton Town

The season so far has been nothing short of a struggle for Ashton Town. Last season, they were one of many contenders for the title around the festive period, but from their opening six league games this time around, they are yet to get on the board.

They have played the joint-most league games of any side in the First Division North in 2026/27 at the time of writing, alongside Maghull and Holker Old Boys, but haven’t been able to record a win or draw in any of them. Their next fixture sees them travel to face Maine Road - seventh time’s the charm?

5. AFC Bridgnorth too bold to beat

Currently second in the First Division South table, and with a game in hand on early leaders Wolverhampton Casuals, AFC Bridgnorth are thriving in their maiden NWCFL campaign. The WV16 side have recorded three wins and a draw in their first four matches, taking 10 points from an available 12.

It doesn’t take a mathematician to work out that they are yet to suffer a league defeat this season, which is impressive on its own, but they are also the only remaining side in the First Division South not to have given up all the points in a league game this season. It will interesting to see who can slay the dragon.

articles.title: Week 3: Manager Quotes
articles.meta: Mon 17th August 2026 | Manager Reactions | By Jay Cooper
articles.body:
Isuzu FA Vase:

This past weekend saw the return of the Isuzu FA Vase, with a total of 31 NWCFL sides making their competition bow on Saturday. Of those sides, 11 progressed to the next round, including Premier Division Atherton LR on penalties after a 2-2 draw with First Division North side Cammell Laird 1907.

Following such a tense victory, manager Dave Jones said: "I thought we put in a really good performance on and off the ball for 55 minutes. Once they got a goal out of nothing, the picture just changed slightly and gave them something to go after.

"It’s about finding a way to win in cup games and we done that. Full credit to Cammell Laird - I thought they were organised and played really well, and they pushed us all the way. We need to kick on now, rest up and go again on Tuesday at home to Chadderton."

Another Premier Division side that came out on top in a Vase outing on Saturday were Trafford. They put Armthorpe Welfare to the sword in a 4-0 away victory, after which manager Tom Baker said: "We're pleased to get into the next round - that was the main objective.

"It's always difficult having two coach journeys over the space of six days. We played against a really good side, who are at the top of their league, and they've had a really good start. We knew the game was going to be difficult, and that we were going to have to apply ourselves properly, but I felt that if we did that, we were going to win the game.

"Being honest, I wasn't happy with the first half performance - I thought we were ambling through the first 45. We got out noses in front, but I felt like we were making it a contest, but if we had put our foot on the gas, we could have got a few goals in the first half.

"I think it took us probably 10 minutes in the second half to find our groove, but then for the next 30 or 35 minutes, we were the dominant team. We started to do the basics really well, which allowed us to create space, and then we showed some real quality in the goals that we scored."

FC St Helens also guaranteed their place in the next round after their 2-0 victory away from home against Ashton Athletic. Following the result, manager Mike Smith said: "It was a performance that started with a little bit of nerves.

"But we grew into the game and settled down once we scored the first goal. Our second half performance was really good, and we played the majority of it in Ashton Athletic's half of the pitch.

"It was controlled performance and a good, much-needed win."

Finally from the Vase, in something of an upset, First Division South side Barnton knocked of Premier Division Irlam to secure their place in the hat for the next round. Following the whistle, manager Lewis Wood called it a "huge result for the lads!

"A massive win for us against Irlam, who are a strong team and a league above us. The boys showed incredible character, effort and belief from start to finish.

"Credit to every player and every member of the club who was involved. We’ve shown exactly what it means to be a Villager this weekend. What a performance. What a result!"

Premier Division:

Away from the cup contests of the weekend, there was a handful of league action to speak of, including at the home of Chadderton. They welcome Nelson to the Emplas Commercial North Stadium, and saw them off with a 2-1 win, after which, joint-manager Ben Greenidge said: "We went into the game Saturday off the back of two very good midweek training sessions.

"We knew the threat Nelson had in targeting their big man up top, and the boys handled him very well. We needed a fast start and we got exactly that; a great goal in the first couple of minutes finished off by the returning Lazenbury. We weathered a load of corners against us in the first half and went in at half time 1-0 up.

"In the second half, we asked questions of their defence by putting it on them from throw-ins etc, and that's where our second goal came from. A great finish from captain Luke!

"An unforced error with 10 minutes to go gave them a penalty, which Ollie saved tremendously, put they reacted quickest, scoring from the rebound. It made the last five minutes of the game a bit nervy, when we should have been seeing the game out comfortably at 2-0, but we got the three points. Now, it's onto Tuesday away at Atherton LR."

First Division North:

Also in league action were Garstang, in the First Division North. Aided by a Weslie Bajraliu hat-trick, they recorded a 3-0 home win over divisional newcomers AFC Knowsley. After full-time, gaffer Guy Heffernan said: "First of all, it’s great to get on the board, and gain some points - but we should have scored more!

"We missed a penalty, and missed some guilt-edge chances that we should have punished AFC Knowsley for. Fair play to our visitors - they never stopped, and they have some decent players.

"But overall, it's a massive three points for us, but we need to find some consistency now, and keep gaining points going forward."

articles.body:
ISUZU FA VASE FIRST QUALIFYING ROUND

Trafford's first FA Vase tie since 2007 saw them cruise into the next round after a 3-0 win at Armthorpe Welfare. Bile Ahmed put them ahead on the stoke of half time and added the third in the final minute, with Kyle Worsley getting the other for Trafford midway through the half.

Dudley Town are also through after a 3-0 win over Alsager Town, but the biggest win of the day belonged to Eccleshall who beat Allscott Heath 4-0.

First Division South side Barnton pulled off a shock as they won 2-1 away at Premier Division side Irlam. Another win against a higher side came as First Division North side Colne won 2-1 at Premier Division Barnoldswick Town.

FC St Helens are safely through after a 2-0 win at Ashton Athletic with Darwen also pulled off a fine away win as they won 2-1 at NCEL side Winterton Rangers. A big away win saw Litherland REMYCA win 4-1 at Maine Road, Cameron Taylor scoring twice for Remy.

Five games went to penalties with four of our sides progressing. First Division South side Telford Town beat Midland Premier side Darlaston Town 6-5 from the spit after a 1-1 draw, with Foley Meir winning 4-2 on penalties after a goalless draw with Redditch Borough.

Atherton LR surrendered a two goal lead to draw 2-2 with Cammell Laird 1907 but won 3-1 from the spot, whilst Charnock Richard drew 1-1 at Appleby Frodingham before winning 4-3 on penalties.

The only side not to progress were Euxton Villa, who conceded in stoppage time to draw 2-2 at Retford before losing 6-5 from the spot.

Abbey Hulton United won 3-0 at Stafford Town with Wythenshawe Town winning by the same scoreline at Cheadle Heath Nomads. Wednesfield Community went down 4-1 at home to Sutton United, with Studley beating Market Drayton Town 3-1. Northwich Victoria were 2-0 winners at New Mills.

Former NWCFL side Kendal Town beat Steeton 2-1, with Flixton losing their first Vase game since reformation as they lost 4-2 at home to Worsborough Bridge Athletic. Two time finalists Glossop North End went down 2-0 at home to Staveley Miners Welfare, with Boldon Community Association beating Longridge Town 2-1.

PREMIER DIVISION .

There were just three games in the Premier Division this afternoon with Burscough's 100% winning start coming to an end with a 2-1 home defeat by Droylsden..Cody Artwell and Jordan Barnet scored either side of half time for the Bloods, with Deacon Smalley grabbing a consolation in stoppage time.

It was the same scoreline at Chadderton who beat Nelson 2-1, with the other game ending 1-1 between Abbey Hey and Prestwich Heys, both goals there coming in the first half.

There is one more Premier Division game of the day as FC Isle of Man host Ramsbottom United. .

FIRST DIVISION NORTH

Garstang won their first game of the season with a 3-0 win at home to AFC Knowsley. After five successive losses, it was a hat-trick from Weslie Bajraliu that proved the difference.

Brandon Collins grabbed a brace for Holker Old Boys as they beat Ashton Town 3-0, with Nathan Salisbury also scoring twice for Halewood Apollo in their 4-2 win at Thornton Cleveleys.

Spencer Lucas hit two for Fulwood Amateurs as they won 4-1 at Ashville, with Maghull coming from behind to win 2-1 at Uppermill, a result that moves them top of the table.

FIRST DIVISION SOUTH

AFC Bridgnorth made it three wins from four games as they came from behind to beat Crewe 4-1, Nehemia Zazi hitting two late goals for the Shropshire side.

Shawbury United beat Widnes 3-2 in an extraordinary game with all goals coming in the first half, the home side taking the lead at the break after trailing when the added time board went up.

Bilston Town won 3-0 at Brereton Social, whilst Wolverhampton Casuals top the table after a 1-0 win at Dawley Town.
